newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia stocks mixed, bourse correction goes on.
newsitem.headline: Estonia stocks mixed, bourse correction goes on.

text.p: Shares on the Estonian stock exchange were mixed by the close on Thursday as prices tried to move higher but failed to overcome a correction.
Dealers were not optimistic for a recovery on Friday ahead of the long midsummer weekend.
Total turnover on the main list was 59.7 million kroons and the Talse index slipped 0.79 percent to 266.70.
The market has undergone a correction amid profit taking following a rally late last week and at the start of this week.
"Prices tried to rise in the morning but fell back with some investors profit taking in the afternoon," one dealer said.
With a long weekend of four days coming up, dealers did not think the bourse would attempt to rally again.
"Tomorrow will not really help as people will be getting out of the city early for the long weekend followed by a three day week," another trader said.
Hansapank was the most active stock with 26.4 million kroons traded to drop 1.55 kroons to close at 141.20 kroons.
Forekspank turned over of 11.1 million kroons and lost two kroons to finish at 188.50 kroons.
Hoiupank announced after the bourse closed that it was going to postpone its move to the Lithuanian market and focus on the Russian and Ukrainian banking markets.
However, dealers did not believe that the change of plans will affect the stock's price.
"It will make some investors reconsider their involvement with the bank," one dealer said.
"But the bank's results from the local market are strong and its price will not be affected by the news," he added.
The free market saw trade of 10.1 million kroons with privatisation vouchers the most active with trade of 3.9 million kroons to be 0.08 kroons higher on 0.288 kroons.
Rakvere traded down to end at 13.40 kroons, 0.65 kroons lower with 1.4 million kroons traded.
"It was the suspension news that took the stock lower, but there were plenty of buyers around 13.30, so I would not be surprised if it regained what it lost today," one dealer said.
"The company is still good and it was the action of one trader and his clients that caused the suspension," another trader said.
